newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-IRABU LIVES UP TO BILLING AS YANKS CRUSH TIGERS 10-3.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-IRABU LIVES UP TO BILLING AS YANKS CRUSH TIGERS 10-3.

text.p: Hideki Irabu delivered on Thursday, thrilling a Yankee Stadium crowd of more than 50,000 by using his impressive repertoire to hold down the Tigers for 6 2/3 innings as New York routed Detroit 10-3.

Irabu, making his long-awaited major league debut, gave up two runs and five hits with four walks and nine strikeouts before leaving to a standing ovation in the seventh. Fans coaxed him out for a curtain call and he doffed his cap on the dugout steps of baseball's most famous ball park.

"This is my first experience to pitch in front of a crowd like this and it was good," Irabu said through an interpreter. "The experience was more than I ever dreamed about. I felt I had to accommodate (the fans') expectations."
Irabu struck out four of the first six batters he faced. He ran into trouble in the third, walking Curtis Pride and issuing singles to Raul Casanova and Deivi Cruz as the Tigers took a 1-0 lead.
Irabu, 28, struck out the side in the fourth and gave up another run in the fifth, but he retired the last six hitters he faced and threw 61 of 98 pitches for strikes.
"Irabu was confident to throw any of his pitches for strikes," manager Joe Torre said. "You just have to look forward to next time he pitches. He's wearing our uniform and he's part of the team."

Derek Jeter had four hits and three runs scored, and Tino Martinez contributed a three-run homer, his 29th, for the winners, who scored four runs in the third, and three more in both the fifth and sixth innings.
"We got him some runs and it made him relax," Martinez said of Irabu. "He showed a lot of composure and maturity."

In Boston, the Red Sox 'walked' to victory over the Toronto Blue Jays as Nomar Garciaparra drew a bases-loaded walk with two outs in the bottom of the 11th to force in the winning run in an 8-7 victory.

Mike Stanley drew a walk against Mike Timlin to start the 11th and moved to second on Troy O'Leary's sacrifice. One out later Darren Bragg was intentionally walked. Jesus Tavarez walked to load the bases and Garciaparra walked on five pitches, forcing in Stanley with the winning run.
Vaughn Eshelman (3-3) worked the 11th for the victory.
Timlin, who gave up an RBI-single to Mo Vaughn in the bottom of the 10th that re-tied it 7-7, blew his fourth save of the season. Timlin (2-1) had not allowed a run in his previous six outings.
"I take responsibility for this loss," Timlin said. "I threw some close balls, but you're not going to get the balls that are just off the plate if you're not throwing strikes consistently."

In Seattle, Joey Cora had four hits and capped a seven-run fifth inning with a three-run homer and Jay Buhner added three hits and two RBI as the Seattle Mariners continued their mastery over the Texas Rangers with a 12-9 victory.

Alex Rodriguez went 4-for-5 and Dan Wilson added three hits and two RBI for the West-leading Mariners (50-38), who have won six of seven meetings with the Rangers this year and are 35-8 against them over the last four seasons.

Jamie Moyer (9-2) won his fifth straight. Norm Charlton struck out Will Clark with two runners on in the ninth for his 13th save. Juan Gonzalez hit a three-run homer and drove in five for Texas, who fell six games behind Seattle.

In Kansas City, Ray Durham homered, doubled, singled, scored a career-high four runs and added three RBI to lead the Chicago White Sox to a 6-3 victory over the Kansas City, spoiling Tony Muser's first game as Royals manager.
Frank Thomas added two hits and also knocked in three runs for the White Sox, who posted their fourth straight win.
Jaime Navarro (7-7) allowed three runs in five innings to post the win. Roberto Hernandez got the final three outs, striking out Tom Goodwin with two men on for his 21st save.
At Minnesota, Brad Radke allowed two runs over seven innings to win his seventh straight start as the Minnesota Twins defeated the Cleveland Indians 8-2.

Radke (11-5) gave up eight hits, walked two and struck out five and combined reliever Greg Swindell to shut down Indians catcher Sandy Alomar, who went 0-for-4 to end his 30-game hitting streak one game shy of Nap Lajoie's 1906 club record.
"I always put in my mind if it ends tonight, it ends," said Alomar, the MVP of Tuesday's All-Star game, about the streak. "Tonight was one of those nights I felt anxious about.
"I feel like it's a load off my back. I mean I gave it everything I've got. I didn't have any bat speed tonight."
At Oakland, Allen Watson threw six strong innings and Jim Edmonds drove in three runs as the Anaheim Angels maintained their domination of the Oakland Athletics with an 8-4 victory.
The Angels (45-42) have won all seven meetings with Oakland (37-53) this year.

Watson (8-5) tied a career high with eight strikeouts, retiring 15 of 16 batters into the sixth inning after giving up a run in the first. The left-hander tired in the seventh, giving up back-to-back homers to Jason Giambi and Scott Spiezio before giving way to reliever Rich DeLucia.
Edmonds, Jack Howell, and Chad Kreuter homered for the Angels.
